title: Pullback is t-exact for the standard constructible t-structures
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum $p,a,q,k_0,k$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\neq p$, an algebraic closure $\Qlb$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ contained in $\Qlb$, and let $\Lambda\in\{E,\Qlb\}$, with the rationalized category $D^b_c(-,E)$ and the common-stage category $D^b_c(-,\Qlb)$ [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients]. Let $h:W\to X$ be a morphism of finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], and let $Lh^*:D^b_c(X,\Lambda)\to D^b_c(W,\Lambda)$ be the derived pullback [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. Use on both sides the standard pair [def-weil-constructible-standard-tstructure], its constructible heart $\Sh_c(-,\Lambda)$ [def-weil-constructible-heart] and the cohomology functors $\mathcal H^j$ [prop-constructible-truncations].

Then $Lh^*$ is $t$-exact: $Lh^*D^{\le0}_c(X,\Lambda)\subset D^{\le0}_c(W,\Lambda)$ and $Lh^*D^{\ge0}_c(X,\Lambda)\subset D^{\ge0}_c(W,\Lambda)$. Consequently $Lh^*$ restricts to an exact functor $\Sh_c(X,\Lambda)\to\Sh_c(W,\Lambda)$, and for every $K\in D^b_c(X,\Lambda)$ and $j\in\mathbf Z$ the truncation maps induce a natural isomorphism $\mathcal H^j(Lh^*K)\cong Lh^*\mathcal H^j(K)$. In particular, for a geometric point $\bar x:s=\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ [def-weil-geometric-point] and the point-fibre functor $\operatorname{Fib}_s$ [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point], $\operatorname{Fib}_s(L\bar x^*\mathcal H^j(K))\cong\mathrm H^j(\operatorname{Fib}_s(L\bar x^*K))$, and for $\mathcal F\in\Sh_c(X,\Lambda)$ the complex $\operatorname{Fib}_s(L\bar x^*\mathcal F)$ is concentrated in degree zero. At $\Qlb$ all these maps are the scalar extensions of the corresponding maps at a common finite coefficient-field stage.

source.place: Definition 6.8.10 and Proposition 6.8.11(3) (constructible $\mathcal O_E$-complexes are the bounded ones with constructible cohomology sheaves, locally $\Lambda\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}\mathcal O_{E,X}$ on strata), Remark 6.8.15 ($f^*K=f^*_{\mathrm{naive}}K\otimes_{f^*_{\mathrm{naive}}\Lambda_X}\Lambda_Y$), and Proposition 6.8.14(2) for rationalization; the t-exactness is the agent's reading of these places.

proof.text: The structure maps to $\operatorname{Spec}k$ and [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian, lem-fin-finite-type-fibre-dimension-bound] make $X,W$ Noetherian and finite-dimensional; a field is Noetherian and its spectrum is quasi-compact of dimension zero. Also $\ell$ is invertible. Apply [lem-a1-integral-stratum-chart-restrictions]: for each integral $K$, choose its exact stratum-cover restrictions $C_V(P)=B_V\otimes_R P^\bullet$, retaining any cohomological interval $[a,b]$ for $K$. This supplies constructibility, linear exactness of $Lh^*$ and its comparison on the actual base-changed charts.

On each primed chart, the restriction square identifies $Lh^*K$ with $Lg^*C_V(P)$. By [lem-a1-completed-perfect-scalar-pullback] this is $C_{V'}(P)$ and has cohomology only in $[a,b]$. Exact chart restrictions and [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-stratum-detection] therefore give $\mathcal H^j(Lh^*K)=0$ outside $[a,b]$. Boundedness lets us take $b=0$ or $a=0$ for either integral standard half [def-weil-constructible-standard-tstructure].

Apply [lem-a1-texact-coefficient-stage-descent] to these integral functors for every finite coefficient field. [lem-weil-pbc-integral-stratified-perfect-characterization] identifies the integral categories; [prop-weil-pbc-integral-tstructure] gives their bounded standard structures. Raw rationalization and its triangles are [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi]; halves are the isomorphism closures in the standard-pair definition. Transition exactness is [lem-weil-scalar-extension-exact-triangulated], and [prop-constructible-truncations] supplies scalar-compatible bounded truncations. The pullback beta maps and unit/tower equations are [lem-pur-integral-operations-scalar-extension]; their termwise scalar maps commute with shifts. The fractions and conjugated arrows in [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom, def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients] are exactly this descent. It gives both required inclusions, exact hearts and the canonical cohomology isomorphisms, with all scalar squares.

Apply Step 3 also to $\bar x:s\to X$, since $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$ is finite type. Whisker its cohomology comparison by $\operatorname{Fib}_s$ and compose with the canonical realization comparison of [lem-a1-point-realization-standard-cohomology]. This gives exactly the displayed point-fibre isomorphism. Both functors send hearts to degree zero, giving concentration. Composition of their scalar squares gives the final common-stage clause.
